research_scope: Five manually reviewed contextual aliases consolidating monic polynomial, formal derivative, residue field, ideal acting on a module, and generated submodule, while maintaining all stricter source conditions.

aliases.reason: Both source contexts use the standard leading-coefficient-equals-one predicate for a polynomial over a commutative unital coefficient ring. The étale polynomial's quotient and the minimal polynomial's irreducibility are additional constraints, not part of this shared prerequisite. Compared the entire source for 'monic polynomial f' against canonical candidate 'monic polynomial'; source phrasing remains immutable.

Both phrases refer to coefficientwise algebraic formal differentiation D(Σa_iX^i)=Σi a_i X^(i-1) over a commutative unital coefficient ring. It is not an analytic derivative; the standard étale map's unit condition in a quotient remains separate. Compared the entire source for 'formal polynomial derivative f′' against canonical candidate 'formal derivative f′'; source phrasing remains immutable.

The residue field of a commutative local ring (R,m) is precisely R/m. That R/m is a field follows from maximality of m; it is not an arbitrary quotient ring and no prime localization is presumed when m is already maximal. Compared the entire source for 'R/m' against canonical candidate 'residue field of a local ring'; source phrasing remains immutable.

For a commutative ring R, the submodule IM is generated by products i·m; taking the ideal I^n instead of I yields (I^n)M as a special instance of the same general ideal-action-on-module construction. Ideal multiplication and forming quotient modules remain separate. Compared the entire source for 'submodule IM generated by products I·M' against canonical candidate 'I^n M'; source phrasing remains immutable.

The directed-colimit relation submodule is the submodule spanned by a specified (possibly infinite) set of relation elements in a direct sum, exactly the general generated-submodule construction. In the finite-generator source the subset is finite, which specializes the same general concept; the quotient imposed by relations is an additional operation. Compared the entire source for 'submodule generated by the differences ι_i(m)−ι_j(μ_ij(m))' against canonical candidate 'R-linear span of generators m_1,…,m_n'; source phrasing remains immutable.
